body:
Reasons Detective: 1. "I think our school should plant a garden in the empty space behind the gym." 2. A garden is an outdoor classroom; kids who grow vegetables are more likely to try them; it would make the space more beautiful. 3. Measuring bean plants in math, watching a plant's life cycle in science, and the cousin's class charting sunflowers. 4. First, For example, Also, Finally, For all these reasons (any three). 5. "For all these reasons, a garden would make our school a better place to learn and grow." 6. Answers vary; look for a reason named and a sensible idea for stronger evidence (for example, a fact about how many students would use the garden).
Should Recess Be Longer?: No single answer. A strong piece states the opinion first, gives two or more reasons with an example each (focus after moving, exercise and health, solving problems with friends), uses linking words, and restates the opinion at the end.
Which Class Pet Should Room 12 Choose?: Either opinion can earn Advanced. Goldfish facts that support it: quiet, lives 10 years or more, can be left over a weekend with an automatic feeder, students can study water and fish. Guinea pig facts: can be gently held, makes wheeking sounds, students learn to care for it daily. Strong pieces may also use a fact against the other choice (a guinea pig cannot be left alone over a weekend; a goldfish cannot be held).
Scoring tip: on the evidence criterion, a reason supported only by feelings ("fish are cute") is Developing; a reason supported by a fact from the sheet is Proficient; a fact that is explained ("so nobody has to take it home") is Advanced.
title: Answer key: Opinion Writing
